description: Logarithm of the absolute value of the gamma function, log|gamma(x)|, for real x

tolerance.reason: For x > 0 the value is well conditioned once x - 1 and x - 2 are formed exactly (Sterbenz's lemma near the zeros at 1 and 2, where careful implementations such as fdlibm and Boost expand in x - 1 and x - 2; taking log(gamma(x)) there instead loses everything), and Stirling's series for large x costs a few ulps. For x < 0 the reflection formula log(pi / |sin(pi x)|) - log Gamma(1 - x) subtracts two terms; rounding them costs (|term 1| + |term 2|) / |result| times 2^-53, at most 664 on this grid (x = -2.75, near the zero at -2.7477), so up to 7.4e-14 is unavoidable. 2e-13 allows 2.7x that and matches the quantile tolerances. SciPy's worst error is 1.8e-15 except at 8 of the 12 points next to 1 and 2, where it loses digits as log(gamma(x)) would: 1.5e-12 at 1 +- 1e-5, up to 8.0e-7 at 1 +- 1e-10 and 2 - 1e-10, and 29% at the double nearest 2 - 1e-15 (the series DLMF 5.7.3 confirms mpmath)

grid: x = -30..180 step 0.25 (poles at 0, -1, ..., -30) and +-10^k for k = -300..-10 step 10 (the gamma grid), plus 10^k for k = 0..300 step 10, x = 1e305, 2e305, 2.5e305, 2.6e305, 1e306, 1e307, 1e308 and the largest double (log Gamma overflows above about 2.55e305), 1 +- d and 2 +- d for d in {1e-5, 1e-10, 1e-15} (rounded to doubles), and x = -100.5, -1000.25, -10000.5, -1000000.5, -999999999999999.5
